why: The Cloud Core decides what the owner may ASK for; the device decides what it will DO.
Until 2026-09-14 each half kept its own list: the Cloud Core's app allowlist had six
names, the device's had seven (mspaint), and the Cloud Core's terminal vocabulary was two
commands against the device's eight patterns. Nothing read the other half, so a name the
owner could say was refused by the device and a command the device would run could not
be said. This file is the one place both lists are written; a Python test and a C# test
each hold their own side equal to it (the file-search-roots discipline, B03).

processes.stop_policy: only an image in `applications` above (never a system process); WM_CLOSE first, terminate only with force

services.restart_policy: only a service named in `restartable`; restarting needs an elevated companion (UAC) and is refused with permission_denied otherwise

read_by: services/api/app/operator/allowlists.py (the Cloud Core's aliases, Turkish names and terminal vocabulary)
devices/windows-agent/src/PagentOS.SessionCompanion/Operator/OperatorCapabilities.cs (DefaultApplications, the process stop policy, the service restart policy)
